title: Week 7 Warm-Ups
intro: Three short review questions each day: two free-response and one multiple-choice. Every question comes from a section completed before the section scheduled for that day.

instances.label: Original
instances.stem_html: Lena walks beside a motorized cart in the school hallway, matching its speed. She says, “The cart stays beside me.” A student standing in the doorway says, “The cart moves east.” Name each student’s reference frame and explain why both descriptions can be correct.

instances.label: Original
instances.stem_html: A small sled slides across the gym floor. A rope pulls it with 26 N east, a second rope pulls with 9 N west, and friction acts with 7 N west. Find the net horizontal force, including direction. Draw one arrow representing the resultant force.

instances.label: Original
instances.stem_html: After one quick push, a puck glides right across nearly frictionless ice at a constant speed. Which statement best describes the puck’s horizontal net force after the hand is no longer touching it?
choices: The hand must still be pushing the puck to the right.
An inertia force pushes the puck forward.
A moving puck must have a larger rightward force.
The horizontal net force is approximately zero.
Gravity provides the forward force.

instances.label: Original
instances.stem_html: A hanging laboratory object weighs 36 N. It is motionless while two vertical spring scales support it. One scale reads 14 N upward. What should the other scale read? Explain using the total upward and downward forces.

instances.label: Original
instances.stem_html: A student stands still on a moving escalator. Describe the student’s motion relative to the escalator step and relative to the building floor. Why is the phrase “the student is not moving” incomplete?

instances.label: Original
instances.stem_html: A tiny camera is attached to a rolling robot. In its video, a sticker on the robot stays in the same location even as the robot crosses the classroom. Which reference frame explains why the sticker stays in one place?
choices: A student watching from the doorway
The camera moving with the robot
The classroom floor
A stationary camera mounted on a wall
A student standing beside the robot’s path

instances.label: Original
instances.stem_html: During a lab trial, a cart rolls 720 cm along a straight track in 12 seconds. Calculate its average speed in cm/s and in m/s. Explain why this average does not tell us the cart’s speed at every instant.

instances.label: Original
instances.stem_html: One lab partner measures a moving robot’s position using tape marks on the classroom floor. Another measures the distance from the robot to a sticker attached to its top. Which measurement can show the robot’s motion relative to the room? Explain why.

instances.label: Original
instances.stem_html: A swimmer travels 120 m in 30 s. A speed sensor reads 5 m/s just as the swimmer finishes. Which statement is correct?
choices: The average speed is 5 m/s and the finish-line speed is 4 m/s.
Both speeds are 5 m/s.
The average speed is 4 m/s and the finish-line speed is 5 m/s.
The average speed is 120 m/s.
No average speed can be calculated from these measurements.

instances.label: Original
instances.stem_html: An RC car travels east at 3 m/s. It turns a corner and travels north at 3 m/s. Compare its speed before and after the turn. Compare its velocity, and explain your reasoning using direction.

questions.topic: How changing a force changes net force

instances.label: Original
instances.stem_html: A person pushes a shopping cart to the right with a force of 22 N while friction acts left with 8 N. Draw the horizontal forces and calculate the net force. If friction increased to 22 N while the push stayed the same, what would the new net force be? Would the cart necessarily stop immediately? Explain.

instances.label: Original
instances.stem_html: Jay and Mei each travel 50 m in a straight-line skateboard run. Jay takes 10 s and Mei takes 8 s. Which statement is supported by the measurements?
choices: Jay averages 5 m/s and is faster than Mei.
Jay averages 8 m/s.
Mei averages 6.25 m/s, but Jay is faster.
Their average speeds are equal because the distances are equal.
Mei averages 6.25 m/s and is faster than Jay, who averages 5 m/s.

instances.label: Original
instances.stem_html: A dog runs 40 m east to fetch a ball in 8 s, then returns 40 m west in 12 s. Find the total distance, total time, and average speed for the whole trip. Explain why returning to the start does not make the average speed zero.

instances.label: Original
instances.stem_html: A cyclist stops pedaling on a rough road, and the bicycle gradually slows. A friend says, “It slows because it runs out of motion.” Explain what actually causes the change in motion, and predict how the bicycle would behave on a surface with much less friction.

instances.label: Original
instances.stem_html: Which motion is an example of constant speed but changing velocity?
choices: A robot travels around a circular path at a steady 2 m/s.
A robot travels straight north at a steady 2 m/s.
A robot speeds up while traveling straight north.
A robot remains parked beside a wall.
A robot travels straight east while its speed increases.
